forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 Internal Audit 2026/27 Progress and Follow-Up of Recommendations Report
findings.headline: Housing stock condition survey at 87% completion with final tranche underway; capital budget flagged for potential re-purposing toward statutory compliance priorities
findings.detail: The Housing Asset Management audit (2025/26) recommendation on stock condition remains in progress with revised implementation date 31 Oct 2026. Management comments record that as of the survey programme update, 'The Council hold an 87% (existing) housing stock condition statistic. A final tranche of Condition surveys will be underway w/c 22nd June 2026 to bring us to 100%'. Comments also flag that 'capital may be reviewed and re-purposed for elements of statutory compliance/HRB priorities'.
findings.matters: Incomplete asset data (87% at time of report draft) indicates gaps in asset condition planning; capital re-purposing language signals potential shift in spending priorities away from planned maintenance toward statutory/regulatory compliance; relevant to long-term maintenance funding and asset strategy.
findings.figures: 87% housing stock surveyed; final tranche to achieve 100%; revised implementation date 31.10.26
findings.quote: The Council hold an 87% (existing) housing stock condition statistic. A final tranche of Condition surveys will be underway w/c 22nd June 2026 to bring us to 100% ... capital may be reviewed and re-purposed for elements of statutory compliance/HRB priorities.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 Internal Audit 2026/27 Progress and Follow-Up of Recommendations Report
findings.headline: Regulator of Social Housing completed inspection in June 2026 and approved new governance Terms of Reference following independent review
findings.detail: On 23 June 2026, the Regulator of Social Housing observed a Housing and Homeless Advisory Board meeting and approved new Terms of Reference following independent review by DTP. The review found that existing governance 'should be strengthened to align with regulatory expectations'. The council's social housing regulatory programme audit (2025/26) contains multiple in-progress recommendations relating to action tracking, evidence retention and knowledge transfer. A post-inspection improvement plan is ongoing.
findings.matters: Regulatory inspection of social housing provider is material compliance event; new governance framework indicates regulatory engagement and potential compliance gaps; ongoing improvement plan signals regulatory oversight of housing operations.
findings.figures: RSH inspection 23.06.26; 5 Social Housing Regulatory Programme audit recommendations; 4 recommendations not yet due, review completed by 31.8.26 and 31.10.26
findings.quote: The Regulator of Social Housing (RSH), on 23rd June 2026. Independent review by DTP identified that the ToR should be strengthened to align with regulatory expectations. The new ToR provide a clearer remit, improved reporting aligned to Consumer Standards and stronger governance discipline.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 Internal Audit 2026/27 Progress and Follow-Up of Recommendations Report
findings.headline: Landlord health and safety audit identified a control gap: remedial actions are tracked in two separate systems with no reconciliation, creating gaps in the auditable record
findings.detail: Two medium-priority recommendations from the 2022/23 Landlord Health and Safety audit, originally due Dec 2022, remain overdue with revised date Sept 30, 2026. Management comments identify that remedial actions from water hygiene monitoring are managed through a contractor's 'Remedial Misc Works' process outside the ZetaSafe dashboard system used to identify actions. Management acknowledges 'it has created a disconnect between the system used to identify actions and the system used to manage their completion, resulting in gaps within the auditable record' and describes this as 'a weakness in our record management and assurance processes'.
findings.matters: Control weakness in housing landlord compliance function is material to asset management and tenant safety assurance; timing coincides with active engagement by Regulator of Social Housing (inspection June 2026); gaps in auditable records are relevant to regulatory compliance and audit trail requirements.
findings.figures: 2 recommendations overdue; originally due 31.12.22, revised to 30.9.26
findings.quote: it has created a disconnect between the system used to identify actions and the system used to manage their completion, resulting in gaps within the auditable record. Accordingly, each outstanding action will be reviewed individually to confirm its current status

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 Internal Audit 2026/27 Progress and Follow-Up of Recommendations Report
findings.headline: Two climate change audit recommendations have been formally removed from the follow-up because no budget was allocated to implement them
findings.detail: Two medium-priority recommendations from the 2025/26 Climate Change audit have been marked as 'risk accepted' and removed from the implementation tracking. The recommendations required funding for equipment to monitor energy use in buildings and development of a climate change spending profile. Management comments record that 'A budget request to purchase equipment to facilitate better monitoring of energy use in our buildings was requested. No budget has been allocated' and that the s151 officer confirmed 'there was no money available to support the service'.
findings.matters: Formal risk acceptance for non-implementation of audit recommendations suggests budget constraints limiting improvement activity; signals tight financial position that may affect other service delivery areas; ESG/environmental compliance implications.
findings.quote: A budget request to purchase equipment to facilitate better monitoring of energy use in our buildings was requested. No budget has been allocated. ... Unfortunately, we were informed that there was no money available to support the service.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 Internal Audit 2026/27 Progress and Follow-Up of Recommendations Report
findings.headline: Nine audit recommendations are overdue, including three high-priority payment system compliance items from 2021/22, with implementation dates repeatedly missed since December 2023
findings.detail: The PCI DSS audit (2021/22) contains three high and medium priority recommendations now overdue by multiple years. Original due date was Dec 2023; subsequent revisions set dates for Feb 2026, May 2026, July 2026 and Sept 2026, all now missed. Current status: PCI policy being finalised, Self-Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ) for payment card compliance 'has not yet been revisited', training material in preparation. The Head of Internal Audit took post in Oct 2025 and reports that while the backlog has reduced, 'the level is still concerning'.
findings.matters: High-priority payment system compliance is material for any organisation taking card payments; pattern of repeated missed deadlines since late 2023 signals systemic implementation or capacity issues; control environment weakness is relevant to financial controls assessment.
findings.figures: 9 overdue recommendations out of 97 total tracked; PCI DSS recommendations original due date 31.12.23 with subsequent revisions to 28.02.26, 31.5.26, 31.7.26, 30.9.26
findings.quote: there are several recommendations that are extremely overdue, whilst the number of outstanding recommendations has significantly reduced following taking on the role of Head of Internal Audit in October 2025, the level is still concerning

daily_post.headline: Market interest rate expectations have reversed; council's under-borrowed strategy faces rising rate risk
daily_post.lead: If the council is forced to borrow at elevated PWLB rates (now 5.28%-6.29% depending on term), the under-borrowed position becomes expensive; the strategy was not hedged against rate rises.
